newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Strike halts domestic flights at Tyumen, Siberia.
newsitem.headline: Strike halts domestic flights at Tyumen, Siberia.

text.p: Air traffic controllers at the west Siberian city of Tyumen began an indefinite strike on Wednesday, closing the airport to domestic flights but not affecting long-distance flights in-transit over Tyumen airspace.

Robert Urtsev, the head of the Russian Air Traffic Centre in Moscow, told Reuters the strikers had begun their action at 08.00 (0400 GMT). Itar-Tass news agency said they were demanding back pay owed since November -- a common problem in Russia.
Though no international flights are scheduled at Tyumen, any charters from abroad would be allowed in, Urtsev said.
The Tyumen controllers are working normally for domestic and international transit routes across their region. Moscow controllers are also assisting on transit flights.
Urtsev said the strike breached International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) rules stipulating that strikers must give seven days' notice before taking action.
Comment from the strikers was not immediately available. - Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
